newsitem.title: ITALY: Priebke must await war crimes trial in Italian jail.
newsitem.headline: Priebke must await war crimes trial in Italian jail.

text.p: An Italian court ruled on Monday that 83-year-old former SS captain Erich Priebke must remain in a Rome military jail while he awaits re-trial for war crimes.
The court rejected a request by Priebke's lawyers that he be freed or released into house arrest. His lawyers had cited his advanced age and the length of his incarceration in Italy.
Priebke, a German, has been detained in Rome since November 1995 when he was extradited from Argentina, where he had lived openly for nearly 50 years.

Italy sought his extradition after Priebke admitted to a U.S. television crew which had tracked him to his home in the Andean resort of Bariloche that he took part in the SS massacre of 335 men and boys in caves near Rome on March 24, 1944.

The court ruled that notwithstanding his age and the amount of time that had passed since the crime, Priebke could try to flee Italy and said there were "secret organisations" which helped former Nazis to hide.
"It's a political, not a judicial decision," defence attorney Giuseppe Naso said.
Priebke was tried last year by judges who ruled he could go free, but the verdict was thrown out on appeal.
No new date has been set yet for his re-trial because Rome's military and civilian courts have both said they do not have jurisdiction to hear the case.
Italy's highest court, the Court of Cassation, will ultimately decide the question of jurisdiction. It will hear arguments on the matter next month.
Priebke has admitted he shot two people at the Ardeatine Caves and crossed off names from a list as victims were led inside. He argues he had to follow orders or be killed himself.
The massacre, Italy's worst wartime atrocity, was ordered in retaliation for a partisan bomb attack in Rome the day before which killed 33 members of the German occupying forces.
